title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Oil eased to roughly $114/bbl Monday after settling at $116.72 Friday (highest since April), as President Trump signaled he will not strike Iran today, paring back some of Friday's risk premium.

Markets: Gold slipped below $4,000/oz and bitcoin fell to around $80K (weakest in over a month) as traders priced higher odds of a Fed rate hike, with oil-driven inflation risk now outweighing growth worries.
Markets: Asian equities were soft to start the week — Australia's ASX fell, with markets pricing better-than-60% odds of an RBA rate hike, echoing a broader global rates repricing.
Companies: Verizon reports Q3 2026 earnings Monday morning, the first notable print in a heavy week of results that also includes Alphabet, Microsoft, ExxonMobil, Chevron, Coca-Cola and GE Vernova.

Macro/Policy: The Fed's two-day FOMC meeting kicks off this week; markets price roughly 90% odds of a hold on Wednesday but ~78-79% odds of a hike by December — an unusual flip from earlier expectations of cuts, driven by oil-shock inflation risk.

Macro/Policy: Iran-linked oil-supply risk remains the dominant macro driver — Friday's spike to $116.72 Brent (highest settle since April) still frames this week's Fed and inflation debate even as prices ease slightly today.
